newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 3.04 bln stg in February-BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 3.04 bln stg in February-BBA.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the UK private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 3.04 billion stg in February, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said.
This compares with a rise of 2.472 billion in January and an underlying six-monthly average increase of 2.253 billion.
Consumer credit was up a record 626 million stg, well above the recent monthly average.
BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said personal lending rose by over 1.3 billion stg in February, the largest monthly increase since the series began in 1991.

"The growth in consumer credit was particularly striking," he said. "The increase over the month of more than 600 million stg was almost 50 percent above the recent monthly average and another record for the...series."
Mortgage lending rose by 743 million stg, down from a buoyant January figure of 806 million but above the recent monthly average of 659 million.
Lending to the manufacturing sector overall fell by 409 million stg while lending to the financial sector rose by 656 million.
"While the rise in mortgage lending was a little down on the strong January figure, it remained comfortably above the recent average," Sweeney said.
"With lending to industry and commerce fairly flat, borrowing by companies in the financial sector was the other factor responsible for overall lending in growth in February."
